title: Long context 4k-128k bytes on the trained R1.14 models: stability, copying beyond the window, memory and speed
follows: R1.14 (running when this was registered; no R1.14 result was seen)
dispatch: report-only: reuse_run = the R1.14 run, artifact_prefix = r1_14 (the R1.14 checkpoints are evaluated; nothing is trained)
question: Reading test streams of up to 64k bytes (throughput and memory to 128k), does Rouge-LM stay stable far beyond its training segments, keep an advantage over the Transformer's 256-byte window far out, and carry an exact string over 1k bytes in its 16 gated slots?

predictions.C1: expected to FAIL: exact recall needed addressable memory in R1.03; Rouge-LM has only 16 gated slots per layer, trained for next-byte prediction on enwik8, where exact copies over 1k bytes are rare. A FAIL motivates adding R1.03's exact memory to Rouge-LM.
predictions.C2: expected to hold: the gated state keeps its scale over 64k bytes (bias +2 keep gate, LayerNorm on reads); a failure would show drift of the recurrence far beyond the training segments.
predictions.C3: uncertain: holds if R1.14's L3 holds and the advantage does not fade far out.
predictions.C4: analytic: Rouge-LM 1.2 MiB at any length vs 2.5 GiB of KV cache for a full-context 8-layer d=320 Transformer at 128k bytes (reported, not a learned property).
predictions.C5: probe sanity: inside its window the Transformer must copy (gain >= 1 bit/byte). If it does not (C5_probe_broken), the probe is broken and the result is VOID (first decision rule).

prior_art: Passkey / needle-in-a-haystack retrieval (Mohtashami & Jaggi 2305.16300), RULER 2404.06654, long-context evaluation of recurrent models (Griffin 2402.19427, Mamba 2312.00752)
not_claimed: Constant memory is a property of the design, not a result. Only the measured stability, copy gain and far-context BPB are results.
